title: Group dilatations at a closed fibre and their universal property
statement: All group schemes in this statement are schemes [def-pc-scheme] equipped with multiplication, identity and inverse over the indicated base, satisfying the group diagrams (the relative version of [def-sc-group-scheme]). Flatness, smoothness and local finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A Dedekind domain is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ for a Dedekind domain $D$, let $s$ be a closed point of $S$, let $G$ be a flat separated $S$-group scheme locally of finite type, and let $F\hookrightarrow G_s$ be a closed subgroup scheme of its fibre [def-pc-base-change]. There is a flat separated $S$-group scheme $G'$, locally of finite type, and an affine group homomorphism $d:G'\to G$, called the dilatation of $F$ at $s$, with the following properties. It is an isomorphism over $S\setminus\{s\}$ and its special-fibre map factors through $F$. For every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ and every $S$-morphism $f:X\to G$ whose fibre map $f_s$ factors through $F$, there is a unique $S$-morphism $f':X\to G'$ with $df'=f$. The group $G'$ is commutative if $G$ is. The scheme and map have this concrete affine description: on a base neighbourhood where the ideal of $s$ is generated by $\pi$, and on any affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset G$ above it, let $I\subset A$ be the inverse image of the ideal of $F$ in $A/\pi A$. Then $d^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Spec}A[I/\pi]$, where $A[I/\pi]$ is the subalgebra of $A[1/\pi]$ generated by $A$ and the elements $a/\pi$ for $a\in I$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These charts identify with $G$ away from $s$ and define the same scheme for every choice of local generator. Localization to $D_s$ gives the dilatation with the same chart formula over $D_s$. No quasi-compactness of $G$ or $F$ is required.

source.place: BLR 3.2 Propositions 1 and 2, printed pp.63-64; construction on locally Noetherian affine charts, globalized at a closed point of a Dedekind base as in 10.1 Proposition 4 proof, printed p.291. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}D_h$ of $s$ on which its ideal is $(\pi)$ and $V(\pi)=\{s\}$. Here is why this choice exists. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $s$ is finitely generated. By [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] its extension to $D_{\mathfrak m}$ has a generator $a/b$ with $a\in\mathfrak m$, $b\notin\mathfrak m$. Write each of finitely many generators of $\mathfrak m$ as a multiple of $a$ in $D_{\mathfrak m}$, and invert the product $h\notin\mathfrak m$ of the denominators in these equations. Then $\mathfrak mD_h=aD_h$; take $\pi=a$. Its vanishing set is exactly $s$ because it is the extended maximal ideal. Cover $G_V$ by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ on which $A$ is a finitely generated $D_h$-algebra. Their rings are Noetherian: $S$ is locally Noetherian by its single affine Noetherian cover, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies to $G\to S$, and [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] applies to each $U$. For the inverse-image ideal $I\subset A$ of $F\cap U_s$ one has $\pi\in I$ and $I$ is finitely generated. Put $B_U=A[I/\pi]\subset A[1/\pi]$ as in [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring].

source.place: BLR 3.2, construction and Proposition 1, printed pp.62–63; Proposition 2(d), printed p.64. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan, PDF pp.68–70: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Agent-written globalization to a locally finite type Dedekind-base group scheme.

proof.text: The following short ring calculation gives the lifting property needed below. Let $\varphi:A\to C$ send $I$ into $\pi C$, and suppose multiplication by $\pi$ on $C$ is injective. By [lemma-nagata-chart-ring-normal-form], every element of $B_U$ is $x/\pi^n$ with $x\in I^n$. Send it to the unique $c\in C$ with $\pi^nc=\varphi(x)$; existence follows from $\varphi(I^n)\subset\pi^nC$. If $x/\pi^n=y/\pi^m$, [lemma-nagata-chart-ring-fraction-equality] gives $\pi^k(\pi^mx-\pi^ny)=0$ for some $k$. Applying $\varphi$ and cancelling $\pi^{k+m+n}$ proves equality of the proposed images. Addition and multiplication follow after multiplying by the common denominator. This defines the unique $A$-algebra map $B_U\to C$: its value on $a/\pi$ must solve $\pi c=\varphi(a)$. Thus the construction uses divisibility in a torsion-free target, not an unjustified map $A[1/\pi]\to C$.

source.place: BLR 3.2, construction and Proposition 1, printed pp.62–63; Proposition 2(d), printed p.64. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan, PDF pp.68–70: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Agent-written globalization to a locally finite type Dedekind-base group scheme.

proof.text: The rings $B_U$ are flat over $D$. Indeed $A$ is $D$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] applied to $U\subset G$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$. It is $D$-torsion-free: tensor the injection $D\xrightarrow{r}D$, $r\ne0$, with $A$, using the defining injectivity criterion [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Localizing at $\pi$ preserves this property directly: if $r(x/\pi^n)=0$, then $\pi^krx=0$ for some $k$, hence $\pi^kx=0$. The subring $B_U\subset A[1/\pi]$ is consequently $D$-torsion-free. Apply [lem-sfb-dedekind-torsionfree-module-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] to obtain flatness of $\operatorname{Spec}B_U\to S$. If $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, then $B_U$ is generated over $A$ by $a_1/\pi,\ldots,a_r/\pi$, so it is finitely generated over $D_h$, and over $D$ after adjoining $1/h$. Finally $IB_U=\pi B_U$: one inclusion uses $a=\pi(a/\pi)$, the other uses $\pi\in I$. This proves the special-fibre factorization on each chart.

proof.text: For a flat $S$-scheme $T$ with $f:T\to U$ whose fibre over $s$ maps into $F$, cover $T$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Their coordinate rings are $D$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], hence $\pi$-torsion-free by tensoring the multiplication injection as in step 3. (Over $V$, $\pi=a\in D$ is nonzero.) Scheme-theoretic factorization on the fibre says exactly $\varphi(I)\subset\pi C$. Step 2 supplies the unique affine lifts to $\operatorname{Spec}B_U$ via [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. They agree on overlaps: refine an overlap by affine opens, restrict both ring maps, and use the same uniqueness calculation there. They therefore glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Conversely every lift factors through $F$ on the fibre by $IB_U=\pi B_U$. We have proved the universal property on arbitrary flat test schemes mapping to $U$, with no finite type or quasi-compactness assumption on the test scheme.

source.place: BLR 3.2, construction and Proposition 1, printed pp.62–63; Proposition 2(d), printed p.64. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan, PDF pp.68–70: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Agent-written globalization to a locally finite type Dedekind-base group scheme.

proof.text: Glue the affine constructions. For two affine charts $U_i,U_j\subset G_V$, let $W=U_i\cap U_j$. The inverse image of $W$ in each constructed chart is open and flat over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] (restrict a flat map to an open subscheme). Its map to $G$ has special fibre in $F$. The flat-test property of step 4 constructs unique maps between these two inverse images over $W$, after covering $W$ by affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Their composites are identities by uniqueness. On triple intersections both transition composites are lifts of the same map, so they agree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain a scheme $H_V\to G_V$ with these charts and with inverse image of each $U_i$ exactly $\operatorname{Spec}B_{U_i}$. Since $B_U[1/\pi]=A[1/\pi]$ (both contain $A$ and $1/\pi$ and embed in $A[1/\pi]$), this map is the identity over $V\setminus\{s\}$. Glue $H_V$ to $G_{S\setminus\{s\}}$ along this identified open, giving $d:G'\to G$. Its flat-test property glues on these two base opens by the same uniqueness argument and morphism-gluing theorem.

proof.text: The glued $G'$ is flat and locally of finite type over $S$: its chart morphisms have these properties by step 3 and the unchanged charts away from $s$, and both properties can be checked on this open source cover by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. The map $d$ is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], using the constructed affine inverse images on a target affine open cover. Consequently $d$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The composite $G'\to S$ is separated: its diagonal factors as the closed immersion $\Delta_d:G'\to G'\times_GG'$ followed by $G'\times_GG'\to G'\times_SG'$, the pullback of the closed immersion $\Delta_{G/S}$. This factorization is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. The required universal property for smooth $X$ follows from the flat-test property and [lem-pc-smooth-flat].

source.place: BLR 3.2, construction and Proposition 1, printed pp.62–63; Proposition 2(d), printed p.64. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan, PDF pp.68–70: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Agent-written globalization to a locally finite type Dedekind-base group scheme.

proof.text: Construct the group operations using the proved flat-test property, rather than applying a smooth-test property to $G'$. Finite powers of $G'$ over $S$ are flat, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-pc-flat-compose]. The map $G'\times_SG'\xrightarrow{d\times d}G\times_SG\xrightarrow{m}G$ has special fibre in $F$, since $F$ is a subgroup; it lifts uniquely to $m':G'\times_SG'\to G'$. Likewise the inverse $i\circ d$ lifts from the flat scheme $G'$, and the identity $e:S\to G$ lifts from $S$. Thus $d$ respects all three operations. On $(G')^3$ the two associativity composites have equal composites with $d$, hence are equal by uniqueness of the lift of that one map. The two unit composites on $G'$ and the two inverse composites similarly become the corresponding equalities in $G$ after $d$, so uniqueness proves all the group axioms. If $m$ is commutative, $m'$ and $m'\circ\mathrm{swap}$ have the same composite with $d$, and uniqueness proves commutativity.

proof.text:
The construction is independent of the local generator: if $\pi'=u\pi$ with $u$ a unit, then $a/\pi'=u^{-1}(a/\pi)$, so the two subalgebras are literally equal in the common localization. Independence of the chosen neighbourhood and affine cover follows from the two flat-test universal properties: each flat construction uniquely lifts its map to the other, and the two composites are identities by uniqueness. The resulting canonical isomorphisms respect $d$ and the group operations. For localization at $s$, on a chart put $W=D\setminus\mathfrak m$. Directly localizing the generators gives
$$W^{-1}(A[I/\pi])=(W^{-1}A)[(W^{-1}I)/\pi]$$
in $W^{-1}(A[1/\pi])$: generators on the right are $a/(w\pi)=(1/w)(a/\pi)$, and conversely the left is generated by these fractions and $W^{-1}A$. This gives the stated chart formula after base change to $D_s$; group maps restrict to the same maps on these charts. Every construction used set-indexed open covers and finitely many ideal generators on one affine chart at a time. No global finite cover of $G$ or $F$ was used.
